payload.statement: Arg525 sits in the kinase-domain helix that lines the ATP pocket. Replacing its positive charge with a neutral glutamine removes a contact needed to bind ATP, which weakens nucleotide binding and reduces catalytic activity.
payload.would_refute: Ligand-bound experimental structures (e.g. 5P9J, which observes residue 525 with an ATP-site ligand) show the Arg525 side chain more than about 6 Å from any ATP, ATP-analogue, or inhibitor atom. A model of R525Q bound to ATP that keeps the same pocket geometry and contacts as the wild type would also refute it.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: UniProt's annotation for this exact substitution (E2) says it disturbs ATP binding, and InterPro places 517-529 in the active site (E7). Both point directly at ligand contact, which is the most specific evidence on this residue. Still missing: any structure-level check that Arg525 contacts the ATP site (G2), and any measurement of R525Q activity or ATP affinity (G1, G3).

payload.statement: Arg525 is part of the helix within the kinase C-lobe/catalytic region whose buried salt bridges or hydrogen bonds hold the fold together. Losing that network destabilises the helix and the domain, so the protein folds less stably and is degraded or misfolds, which lowers the amount of active BTK.
payload.would_refute: Predicted stability changes (e.g. FoldX or Rosetta ddG on the experimental structures, or on AF-Q06187-F1) show R525Q within about 1 kcal/mol of wild type, with no loss of helix contacts and no change in local backbone dynamics. Simulations of R525Q matching wild-type fluctuation would also refute it, as E10 already reports only local changes for other mutations.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Strong conservation (E11: 0.967) and high predicted pathogenicity (E9, E13, E14) suggest the residue matters for the fold. But these scores do not say how, none of the retrieved studies tests R525Q directly (G1), and E10 reports only local dynamic changes for other clinical BTK variants, which weakens a global fold-loss story.

payload.statement: Arg525 is one of the contact points at the SH2-kinase interface that holds BTK in an autoinhibited or activation-competent arrangement. The Gln substitution breaks this interdomain contact, which changes the conformational switch needed for activation by phosphorylation.
payload.would_refute: Full-length or SH2-kinase structures or models show that Arg525 has no atom within about 4 Å of the SH2 domain, or that its side chain points into the kinase core away from any interdomain surface. Alternatively, R525Q keeps the SH2-kinase interdomain contact network and the activation-loop conformation of wild type in simulation.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The SH2-kinase mechanism (E8) is documented, but for other XLA substitutions in the SH2 domain, not for residue 525 in the kinase domain. No retrieved evidence places Arg525 at that interface (G2), so this is the weakest of the three. It remains worth testing because it is the only one that would explain activation defects without changing the active site.

payload.summary: Three competing mechanisms are recorded for BTK p.Arg525Gln: H1 ATP-site contact loss (ligand_binding, starting rank 1), H2 helix destabilisation (stability_folding, rank 2), and H3 loss of SH2-kinase interdomain contact (domain_interface, rank 3). H1 is favoured because UniProt annotates this exact substitution as disturbing ATP binding (E2). The critical missing evidence is a structural check of whether Arg525 contacts the ATP site (G2) and any direct functional data on R525Q (G1, G3). Each hypothesis has a refutation condition for the next test.

payload.description: For the 120 experimental BTK structures that observe residue 525 with a non-solvent ligand, check whether Arg525 is listed as a neighbour of the bound ligand and at what shortest distance. Tests H1: a contact with an ATP-site ligand supports it; no contact in ligand-bound structures weakens it.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: H1 is the current favourite (starting rank 1), so this test is aimed at the claim most in need of checking. A ligand contact within about 6 Å would support H1 and keep it on top. Ligand-bound structures with the residue more than about 6 Å from every ligand atom would refute H1 and let H2 or H3 move up. The test is silent on H2 and H3 directly (stability and interface are not tested by it), so the ranking can only move through H1. The large set of 120 ligand-bound structures makes a clear result likely. Crystal contacts with soluble analogues limit how much a contact proves.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: Catalogue reports can_run true with 120 ligand-bound structures covering residue 525. Costs 0 compute seconds and 2 tool calls, no approval needed. Uses RCSB PDB data, which is available now.
controls: Negative control: ligands in the same structures that never list the residue as a neighbour.
Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.
Site-state control: structures in which the residue itself is mutated are reported separately.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change for R525Q on the AlphaFold model, with local pLDDT at residue 525 and the values for other disease substitutions at the same residue. Tests H2: a destabilising value supports it; a neutral value (within about 1 kcal/mol) weakens it.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A large destabilising value would raise H2 toward the top and could overtake H1. A neutral value would lower H2 and leave H1 and H3 unchanged. The test says nothing about binding or interfaces, so H1 and H3 stay where they are. FoldX error is near 1 kcal/mol, the same size as the refutation threshold, so an intermediate value would move the ranking little.

per_hypothesis.why: Residue 525 (Arg in wild type) lies within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 8 of 40 ligand-bound experimental BTK structures. The closest contacts are 2.69 Å to ligand 73T (PDB 5T18, 1.5 Å) and 2.92 Å to ligand 7GB (PDB 5P9M, 1.41 Å). The H1 refutation criterion (side chain more than about 6 Å from every ligand atom) was not met. The 25 negative-control ligands never contacted the residue, so the contact is specific rather than a neighbour-list artefact. This supports the premise that Arg525 lines the nucleotide pocket. It does not yet show that the Gln substitution weakens ATP binding, because no R525Q structure was measured and the contacting ligands are inhibitors rather than ATP itself.
T1 measures ligand contact distances, not folding energy or helix stability. No stability value was produced (T2 not run), so the result neither supports nor weakens H2.
T1 only examined ligand contacts in the kinase domain. It did not assess the SH2-kinase interface, and T3 and T4 have not run, so the result neither supports nor weakens H3.

payload.uncertainty: The test is wild-type only: the R525Q mutant was never structurally measured, so the contact loss is inferred, not observed. Contacting ligands are inhibitors and small-molecule crystal contacts, not ATP, so the result shows the residue lines a ligand-binding site, not that R525Q changes binding affinity. The negative-control ligands (25 that never contact the residue) support specificity. Still needed: a ligand-bound R525Q model that is compared with wild type (the H1 refutation test), and a measured ATP Km or activity comparison of recombinant R525Q with wild-type BTK. H2 and H3 remain untested here.

payload.why: Previous favourite H1 (ligand binding) is kept. Direct evidence on R525Q: E2 (UniProt VAR_006255, ECO:0000269) says this substitution disturbs ATP-binding, and T1 shows the wild-type Arg525 sits 2.69 Å from a bound ligand in 5T18 and 2.92 Å from one in 5P9M, with 8 contacting structures and no refutation at the 6 Å threshold. Strongest rival H2 (stability) has only computational support on this exact change (E13 popEVE -6.456, E14 EVE 0.95) and no measured stability value; T1 did not address it. H3 (SH2-kinase interface) has no residue-specific evidence for R525; its support (E6, E8, E12) concerns other substitutions or general domain behaviour. T1 added a measured contact for H1 and left H2 and H3 unchanged. The favourite is unchanged and the previous favourite is not contradicted.

payload.description: Laboratory: express and purify recombinant BTK kinase domain (wild type and R525Q) and run two assays in parallel. (a) Kinase activity with ATP titration to get apparent ATP Km and kcat. (b) Differential scanning fluorimetry to get melting temperature and expression yield. H1 is confirmed if R525Q shows a raised ATP Km or lower activity with a melting temperature close to wild type. H1 is overturned if ATP Km is unchanged. H2 is favoured if melting temperature drops clearly below wild type or the protein is produced at low yield.
payload.why_now: T1 supports H1 but only with wild-type structures, so H1 still lacks a measured effect of R525Q. The ATP-titration and melting-temperature pair separates the two favoured mechanisms directly: H1 predicts altered nucleotide binding with normal folding, while H2 predicts instability. A computational ligand-bound R525Q model would be cheaper, but it cannot separate the mechanisms on its own.

payload.what_to_act_on: The BTK kinase ATP-binding pocket around Arg525 (Q06187), the node where nucleotide binding happens. A molecule would need to restore activity at this node, because the Gln substitution weakens binding. The catalogue direction is loss_of_function with decreased_activity, so the required action is restore.
payload.why: H1 (ligand_binding) is the favoured hypothesis. It says Arg525 lines the ATP pocket and that the neutral Gln removes a contact needed for nucleotide binding, which reduces catalytic activity. T1 places wild-type Arg525 about 2.7 to 2.9 Å from bound ligand in two ligand-bound structures, which supports that pocket location. Every BTK pocket-binding molecule the catalogue lists is an inhibitor, so none of them restore activity. The rows therefore cannot be matched to this node in the restore direction.
payload.rule_why: The protein does too little, so a molecule can only help by bringing the activity back.
payload.direction_basis: No catalog record states a mechanism class for BTK. The IUIS disease label says "agammaglobulinemia", "deficiency", which states that the protein does too little.

payload.text: None of the four rows reads matches. Both are sent so the safety review can record the rejection. cand_01 is the strongest bridge: a two-step pathway link from CD79B, which Reactome places upstream of BTK, to a binding agent, but the molecule's action does not give a direction. cand_02 is a two-step partner link through HSP90AB1, but its inhibitor action lowers HSP90 and nothing states how HSP90 changes BTK activity. cand_03 and cand_04 have the same HSP90 bridge with the same unknown direction, so they are weaker. payload.text:
# Question
What mechanism best explains BTK p.Arg525Gln (Q06187), and which candidate targets and molecules does that mechanism point to? [E2][E4]

# Evidence
ClinVar classes the variant as pathogenic or likely pathogenic, with multiple submitters and no conflicts [E1]. UniProt records the substitution as disturbing ATP-binding [E2] and annotates residues 524–526 as helix [E4] and 517–529 as the kinase active site [E7]. Computational predictions are strongly deleterious: AlphaMissense 0.9976 [E9], EVE 0.95 [E14], popEVE -6.456 [E13]. These are predictions, not measurements. Residue 525 is highly conserved (ScoreCons 0.967) [E11]. The variant is absent from gnomAD v4.1 and no functional assay covers residue 525 [G4]. No retrieved publication studies R525Q directly [G1].

# Agent-generated hypotheses
Three agent-generated hypotheses were formed. H1 (ligand binding): Arg525 lines the ATP pocket, and the Gln substitution weakens nucleotide binding [H1]. H2 (stability): loss of helix contacts destabilises the fold [H2]. H3 (domain interface): the substitution breaks an SH2–kinase contact [H3]. H1 was ranked first at the start [H1].

# Tests considered and the choice
Four tests were considered: T1 (ligand contact), T2 (stability), T3 (structural context) and T4 (structure comparison) [T1][T2][T3][T4]. T1 was chosen for its highest expected learning (0.6), high feasibility (0.9), zero compute seconds and no approval need. T4 was rejected: it needed approval and 120 compute seconds, with only a cached provider available. Safety cleared T1 [T1].

# Result
Residue 525 lies within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 8 of 40 ligand-bound wild-type BTK structures [T1]. The closest contact is 2.69 Å to ligand 73T in PDB 5T18 [E20], and 2.92 Å to ligand 7GB in PDB 5P9M [E21]. The negative-control ligands never contacted the residue [E21]. No structure carried R525Q [G5].

# Updated decision
Favoured before the test: H1. Favoured after: H1. Decision changed: no [H1][T1]. H1 is supported, and H2 and H3 are unchanged because T1 did not test them [H2][H3]. No reopening was needed: the test completed, H1 was not weakened and the favourite did not change.

# Candidates
The direction rule for H1 is decreased activity, so the required action is restore at the ATP-pocket node around Arg525 [R1]. Translator proposals were rejected by safety, with none cleared [G8]. The direction filter ruled out two rows, CD79B-linked and HSP90AB1-linked, as direction_unknown [ruled_out]. The record holds four rows that read unknown on direction [G7]. No candidate is recorded. Any candidate would be a Helix hypothesis, not a recommendation.

# Uncertainty and validation still needed
All R525Q evidence is predictive or inferred. T1 used wild-type structures and inhibitor contacts, not ATP, so it does not show that R525Q weakens binding [E20][E21]. No experiment has been run. H2 and H3 remain untested. Clinical significance was not assessed.

# Next experiment
In the lab, express wild-type and R525Q BTK kinase domain, then run ATP titration to measure apparent Km and activity, and differential scanning fluorimetry for melting temperature [H1][H2]. H1 predicts raised ATP Km with normal folding; H2 predicts a clear drop in melting temperature.
